description.narrative: IFC is considering an investment comprising an up to US$12.0 million A loan and a US$12.0 million subordinated loan from IFC acting as the implementing entity of the International Development Associations Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility for a total financing package of US$24.0 million to Mackie Building Materials (MBM) and MACCEM Industries SL Limited (MACCEM). This will be used to part finance the construction and operation of a cement grinding plant in Hastings, Sierra Leone. This backward integration project is expected to increase supply of locally produced cement and improve cost competitiveness. The project is expected to be supported by an International Development Association Private Sector Window Blended Finance Facility (IDA PSW BFF) as described in the Blended Finance section.

The most significant expected project-level outcomes are: (i) economy-wide effects through substantial value-addition, direct and indirect employment generation, foreign exchange savings while enabling import substitution; and (ii) competitiveness through the localization of a segment of cement manufacturing in Sierra Leone, significantly reducing cement costs, thereby establishing a substantial competitive advantage. In addition to incorporating advanced grinding technology, the project is expected to generate significant demonstration effects by encouraging the adoption of renewable energy solutions, as a portion of IFCs financing will be used for the installation of solar PV.
